newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power prices steady to lower.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were steady to lower Friday in relatively thin trade ahead of expected milder temperatures Monday, industry sources said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Monday peak, non-firm power prices were notionally pegged steady at $17.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP temperatures were expected to be near normal until Tuesday, when some cooling was expected.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday were talked steady at $19.00-22.00, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be slightly below normal Sunday and Monday and rise to slightly above normal next week.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be unchanged at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
In MAIN, Commonwealth Edison's 794 MW Dresden 3 nuclear power unit was expected to synchronize to the electricity grid Friday, returning from a maintenance shutdown which began Oct 26.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday were said to be discussed lower at $16.00-18.00 from $17.00-19.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be near normal Sunday and Monday, then moderate on Tuesday.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co continued to investigate the cause of a shutdown at its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan and had not set a date for the plant to resume electricity production.
The plant was shut Jan 23 after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was also notionally assessed steady at $22.35-22.80 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were pegged lower at $14.00-17.00 through the entire region from $16.00-18.00 in the north and $21.00-23.00 in the south on Thursday, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were assessed lower at $10.00-12.00 through the region from $12.00-13.00 in the north and $13.00-15.00 in the south on Thursday.
In SPP, temperatures were expected to average above normal to much above normal through most of the region through Monday.
